summary: Intermittent timeout spike and throughput variance on Dedicated pool — suspected GPU oversubscription + autoscale sizing mismatch
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent spikes in request timeouts and large variance in throughput from their dedicated GPU pool over the past 48 hours. Impact: ~10-20% of inference requests returned 504/timeout or experienced tail latency > 3s during spike windows. Affects production traffic for Acerta Health (critical monitoring workflows). Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant acerta-prod) running in us-west region; workloads use redwood-v1-small and gptj-6b-quant models. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run steady traffic at 120 RPS with median prompt length ~40 tokens and occasional bursts to 300 RPS for 30-60s; 2) Observe service-level metrics and request-level latencies; 3) Observe timeouts appear after ~6-12 minutes of burst traffic. Observed behavior: Tail latencies and 504s correlate with sudden increase in GPU utilization on a subset of nodes, followed by a short autoscaler cooldown that fails to add capacity quickly enough. Expected behavior: Autoscaler should provision additional nodes/instances to keep latency within SLO during burst events. Logs/metrics referenced: - Host-level GPU utilization spikes to 98% on node gpu-usw-12 between 2026-03-04T21:14 and 21:19 UTC. - Queue depth for tenant acerta-prod increases and head-of-line waiting grows. - Pod-level cgroup metrics show multiple high-throughput jobs colocated on same MIG/instance type. - Autoscale events show scaled-up nodes but with ~45s provisioning lag. Additional notes: Customer asserts they have pinned capacity settings but rely on autoscaling to cover short bursts. They reported the issue via support slack and attached sample request IDs.

investigation_notes: Timeline and findings: - 2026-03-04 21:14 UTC: incident window begins. - Metrics show node-level GPU saturation coinciding with autoscale cooldowns; autoscaler adds nodes ~45-70s after threshold, while tail latency worsens within 15-30s of burst start. - Serving runtime traces show increased KV-cache misses and multiple sessions evicting each other's caches when colocated. - Placement logs show scheduler bin-packing decision preferred filling existing nodes (to save GPUs) for short sessions; this created temporary oversubscription and head-of-line waiting. Hypotheses tested: 1) Noisy neighbor causing GPU oversubscription: reproduced locally by replaying customer burst and co-locating heavy sessions -> reproduced timeout spike. 2) Autoscaler mis-sized: autoscaler threshold and cooldowns are tuned for average sustained load, not short bursts; lowering cooldown or adding predictive burst detection reduces tail latencies in test. 3) Model-specific GPU memory patterns: gptj-6b-quant has higher transient memory allocations leading to context-switch stalls in multi-session colocated scenarios. Actions during investigation: - Collected trace spans and GPU profiled using nvidia-smi and runtime counters. - Created flame graphs for kernel latency for affected nodes. - Cross-referenced scheduler logs (request_ids listed) and found packing decisions at T-30s were the primary correlate. Observed secondary factor: customer's workload uses many short-lived sessions with high token rates which defeats averaging in autoscaler metrics.
resolution_notes: Short-term remediation applied 2026-03-07: - Increased min pool size for Acerta dedicated pool by 2 GPUs to give headroom for bursts. - Applied temporary placement policy to favor node spread rather than aggressive bin-packing for acerta-prod. - Opened alert for GPU saturation >85% sustained for >15s to trigger faster manual/instrumented response. Outcome: Customer confirmed reduced timeouts for subsequent bursts. Permanent fix and follow-ups: - Engineering PR (github.com/redwood/scheduler/PR#819) to add workload-characteristic-aware packing: avoid colocating high-throughput short sessions; add heuristics for transient burst detection. - Autoscaler changes (github.com/redwood/inference/PR#1427): lower cooldown for burst-detection pathway and add predictive scaling using recent rate-of-change of RPS. - Introduce capacity isolation knob per-tenant to reserve spill capacity during bursts; update console UI to show effective reserved headroom. - Post-deploy monitoring: 72-hour canary for changes in us-west with synthetic traffic pattern matching customer bursts. - Create runbook entry and dashboard panel for dedicated pools showing per-tenant GPU packing score and head-of-line queue length. Planned timeline: PR review and canary deploy targeted within 1 week; full rollout after 2-week monitoring window. Follow-up ticket: INT-3498 for autoscaler configuration audit across all Dedicated pools.
